summary: MySeliaSan no longer falls back to a guessable default superadmin credential. EnsureStockSuperadmin silently substituted the literal password 'admin' whenever the configured localAuth.password was empty, which meant a shipped package with a blank config password would have stood up an admin/admin superadmin on the box that controls the entire camera fleet. The password is now resolved as LOCAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD (ops override), then the config value, and otherwise a strong 16-character per-install password generated from crypto/rand - which is printed to the log and saved to INITIAL_ADMIN_LOGIN.txt in the data dir, exactly as mymatasan already does. A generated password is deliberately not re-applied on subsequent boots, so a restart cannot rotate the credential out from under an operator who just read it out of that file. Adds the lock-out recovery path mymatasan already had: a RESET_ADMIN marker file in the data dir (dropped by the Windows installer's 'reset the admin login' option, or by hand) force-resets the superadmin password on next start, re-enabling the account and re-flagging it must-change; the marker is deleted before the reset runs so it can never fire twice. The login screen also asks the server whether federated sign-in is configured (GET /api/auth/config) and hides the 'Continue with myidsan' button when sso.providerBaseUrl is empty, so a standalone install does not present a primary button that cannot work.
compatibility: Existing installs are unaffected: any deployment with a non-empty localAuth.password keeps that password, and an already-taken-over superadmin account is never touched. The behaviour only changes for a config with an EMPTY password - previously that produced admin/admin, and now it produces a generated per-install credential that is printed to the log and written to INITIAL_ADMIN_LOGIN.txt. If you were relying on the admin/admin fallback, set localAuth.password (or LOCAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD) explicitly before upgrading.
